tfResources.role: Primary/core mapping. Maps description, name, kmsKeyId, replicaRegions (as `replica` nested block), and tags. This is the main container resource — it does NOT hold the secret value itself (that's a separate resource, see aws_secretsmanager_secret_version below).

Secondary/companion resource required to carry CfnSecretProps.secretString. In TF, the secret container (aws_secretsmanager_secret) and its value (aws_secretsmanager_secret_version, via secret_string OR the write-only secret_string_wo/secret_string_wo_version fields — all on this SAME resource, linked by secret_id) are always split into two resources, unlike CfnSecret which sets SecretString directly on the single Cfn resource. One CfnSecret with a literal secretString therefore maps to TWO TF resources. NOTE: there is no separate `aws_secretsmanager_secret_wo_version` resource — the write-only variant is just the `secret_string_wo` argument on this resource.

Partial/best-effort mapping for CfnSecretProps.generateSecretString (CfnSecret.GenerateSecretStringProperty). This is a TF *data source*, not a resource — it computes a random password value at plan/apply time (via the GetRandomPassword API) rather than CloudFormation's behavior of generating and persisting the password as the secret's value at resource-create time. The resulting password string must then be wired into aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secret_string (typically wrapped with jsonencode if generateStringKey/secretStringTemplate were used) — there is no single TF resource that reproduces GenerateSecretString's 'generate-and-store' semantics in one step.

attributeNotes:
Field-by-field mapping notes (CfnSecretProps -> TF). Verified against secretsmanager.generated.d.ts (CfnSecretProps at L709; GenerateSecretStringProperty; ReplicaRegionProperty) and provider-aws secretsmanager-secret / secretsmanager-secret-version / data-aws-secretsmanager-random-password index.d.ts.

DIRECT MATCHES (on aws_secretsmanager_secret):
- description -> description (same string, direct).
- name -> name (direct). Note TF also offers name_prefix (no Cfn equivalent; only relevant if generating a random suffix, which CFN does natively when `name` is omitted — see unmappable notes).
- kmsKeyId -> kms_key_id. CASING/TYPE NOTE: Cfn's kmsKeyId is typed `kmsRefs.IKeyRef | string` (can be a live KMS Key construct reference resolved to ARN/ID at synth); TF's kms_key_id is plain `string` only — a construct/token reference must be flattened to its ARN/key-id string (e.g. `${aws_kms_key.x.key_id}`) before being placed in this field.
- replicaRegions (Array<ReplicaRegionProperty{kmsKeyId?, region}>) -> replica (SecretsmanagerSecretReplica[]{kmsKeyId?, region}), a nested block on the SAME resource (not a separate TF resource). Field names match 1:1 after camelCase->snake_case (kmsKeyId->kms_key_id, region->region). Note: TF additionally exposes force_overwrite_replica_secret on the parent resource with no Cfn counterpart (defaults false; irrelevant for create/import path).

VALUE / NESTED-RESOURCE SPLIT:
- secretString -> aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secret_string, keyed by secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.id. For the write-only variant use the secret_string_wo argument (paired with secret_string_wo_version) on the SAME aws_secretsmanager_secret_version resource — there is NO distinct `aws_secretsmanager_secret_wo_version` resource in this provider version (verified: SecretsmanagerSecretVersionConfig exposes secretString, secretBinary, secretStringWo, secretStringWoVersion, versionStages, secretId). This is a genuinely separate TF resource, not a nested block — CfnSecret's single-resource "container + value" model does not exist in the AWS TF provider.
- generateSecretString (GenerateSecretStringProperty) -> best modeled via data.aws_secretsmanager_random_password feeding aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.secret_string. Sub-field mapping (all 8 scalar knobs map 1:1, verified present on DataAwsSecretsmanagerRandomPasswordConfig):
  - excludeCharacters -> exclude_characters (direct)
  - excludeLowercase -> exclude_lowercase (direct)
  - excludeNumbers -> exclude_numbers (direct)
  - excludePunctuation -> exclude_punctuation (direct)
  - excludeUppercase -> exclude_uppercase (direct)
  - includeSpace -> include_space (direct)
  - passwordLength -> password_length (direct)
  - requireEachIncludedType -> require_each_included_type (direct)
  - generateStringKey -> UNMAPPABLE as a field. No TF field embeds the generated password under a named JSON key. Handling: must be reconstructed in the secret_string expression, e.g. `jsonencode({ (generateStringKey) = data.aws_secretsmanager_random_password.x.random_password })`, optionally merged with secretStringTemplate's other keys.
  - secretStringTemplate -> UNMAPPABLE as a field. No TF equivalent; handling: merge the template's static JSON keys with the generated password key via jsonencode(merge(jsondecode(secretStringTemplate), { (generateStringKey) = ... })) when building secret_string.
  - Overall CAUTION: Cfn's GenerateSecretString runs once at secret creation and the generated value is then fixed/immutable in that secret version; the TF data source is refreshed each plan/apply (subject to provider caching behavior), which is a semantic difference the converter should flag, not silently treat as equivalent.

SHAPE / CASING MISMATCH:
- tags: Cfn `Array<cdk.CfnTag>` i.e. `[{Key, Value}, ...]` -> TF `tags?: {[key:string]: string}`, a plain map. Requires reshaping from key/value object array to a map during conversion; the Key/Value field names disappear entirely into map keys/values. Also note TF exposes a separate computed `tags_all` (tags merged with provider-level default_tags) with no Cfn analog.

UNMAPPABLE:
- type (the exact string identifying the third-party/managed external secret partner) -> NO equivalent attribute exists anywhere on aws_secretsmanager_secret, aws_secretsmanager_secret_version, or any other secretsmanager-* TF resource in this provider version (verified: absent from the full attribute list of secretsmanager-secret/index.d.ts). Handling: drop/flag as an unsupported conversion — there is no TF-manageable analog for CFN-managed external secret partner types.
- CfnSecret construct-level conveniences: CfnSecret's `attrId`/`attrArn`/`secretRef` (CFN Fn::GetAtt / Ref outputs) correspond to TF's computed `arn` / `id` attributes on aws_secretsmanager_secret — not a props/config field, so not listed as a resource above, but relevant for downstream references (e.g. IAM policies referencing the secret ARN).

TF-ONLY FIELDS WITH NO CfnSecretProps COUNTERPART (not lost data; noted for completeness): recovery_window_in_days (CFN controls deletion recovery via DeletionPolicy/RemovalPolicy, not a prop), policy (belongs to the sibling AWS::SecretsManager::ResourcePolicy / CfnResourcePolicy, see below), name_prefix, force_overwrite_replica_secret, tags_all, region (provider-level).

NOT MAPPED (deliberately out of scope): secretsmanager-secret-policy (maps to AWS::SecretsManager::ResourcePolicy, a different Cfn resource) and secretsmanager-secret-rotation / data-aws-secretsmanager-secret-rotation (map to AWS::SecretsManager::RotationSchedule) were reviewed and excluded because CfnSecretProps has no resourcePolicy or rotation-related field — those TF resources correspond to sibling Cfn resources (CfnResourcePolicy, CfnRotationSchedule), not to CfnSecret itself.

tfResources.role: Primary/closest equivalent. CfnSecretTargetAttachment's real effect (per its doc comment at secretsmanager.generated.d.ts:801-807) is to add the target database/cluster's connection info into the secret's JSON via a PutSecretValue call, and to expose a .ref (attrId='Id') used to sequence RotationSchedule after the attachment. secretsmanager_secret_version.secret_string is the TF resource that actually writes the JSON payload into the secret, so it plays the equivalent 'populating the secret content' role. secret_id maps from CfnSecretTargetAttachmentProps.secretId. There is no TF-native auto-population from targetId/targetType — the JSON secret_string must be hand-assembled (e.g. via jsonencode({host=..., port=..., engine=..., dbname=...})) referencing attributes pulled from the actual target resource below. NOTE: modern provider versions expose write-only alternatives secret_string_wo (secretStringWo) + secret_string_wo_version (secretStringWoVersion) that hold the JSON without persisting it in state — prefer these over secret_string for connection secrets when the provider version supports them (confirmed present in index.d.ts:32-40).

tfResources.terraformType: aws_docdb_cluster | aws_rds_cluster | aws_rds_cluster_instance | aws_redshift_cluster | aws_redshiftserverless_namespace | aws_docdbelastic_cluster | aws_db_proxy
tfResources.role: Secondary/attribute-source role, NOT a structural 1:1 mapping. CfnSecretTargetAttachmentProps.targetId + targetType select which one of these target resource types the attachment binds to. The L1 CfnSecretTargetAttachment.targetType doc constrains it to 7 values (AWS::RDS::DBInstance, AWS::RDS::DBCluster, AWS::Redshift::Cluster, AWS::RedshiftServerless::Namespace, AWS::DocDB::DBInstance, AWS::DocDB::DBCluster, AWS::DocDBElastic::Cluster). Because TF has no synthetic attachment resource, the concrete TF target resource actually used in the stack must be referenced directly inside secretsmanager_secret_version.secret_string (or secret_string_wo) jsonencode(...) to supply host/port/dbname/engine values CFN would otherwise inject automatically. This is a selector, not a fixed nested prop. DIVERGENCE NOTE: the CDK L2 enum AttachmentTargetType (secret.d.ts:404-429) differs from the L1 doc list — it additionally allows AWS::RDS::DBProxy (=> aws_db_proxy, which exists in this provider) but omits RedshiftServerless::Namespace and DocDBElastic::Cluster; account for aws_db_proxy as a possible attribute source if the source CDK used the L2 SecretTargetAttachment with an RDS_DB_PROXY target.

attributeNotes:
Unmappable / synthetic CFN behavior:
- CfnSecretTargetAttachment has NO real Terraform structural counterpart — there is no aws_secretsmanager_secret_target_attachment resource in the provider (verified by listing lib/). It is a CloudFormation-only orchestration/glue resource whose sole documented job (secretsmanager.generated.d.ts:801-807) is to call PutSecretValue on the secret with the target's connection JSON, and to give downstream resources (RotationSchedule) something concrete to DependsOn for correct ordering. Terraform has no equivalent auto-population mechanism; the conversion must synthesize the behavior manually with secretsmanager_secret_version (or its write-only variant).
- Props confirmed (secretsmanager.generated.d.ts:877-908): CfnSecretTargetAttachmentProps has exactly three required string fields — secretId, targetId, targetType — plus the read-only attribute attrId ('Id', line 839). secretId maps to secretsmanager_secret_version.secret_id. targetId + targetType have NO direct TF field; they only tell CloudFormation's backend which service API to call to fetch host/port/engine/dbname and inject into the secret. In TF this is reconstructed manually by referencing the corresponding target resource's exported attributes (e.g. aws_rds_cluster.endpoint/.port/.master_username, aws_redshift_cluster.endpoint, aws_docdb_cluster.endpoint, aws_redshiftserverless_namespace.*) inside the jsonencode() building secret_string/secret_string_wo. There is no 'targetType' field on aws_secretsmanager_secret_version — selection is implicit in which resource's attributes you reference.
- attrId (CfnSecretTargetAttachment.attrId / .ref = CFN 'Id') is reused by the CDK L2 SecretTargetAttachment as the secret's ARN (secretTargetAttachmentSecretArn / secretArn, secret.d.ts:461-482) purely so other resources depend on the attachment rather than the raw secret. In TF, aws_secretsmanager_secret_version exposes id (import form secret_id|version_id), version_id, arn, and secret_arn (index.d.ts get id()/versionId/arn/secretArn), but downstream resources should generally depend on aws_secretsmanager_secret.arn directly (implicit dep via the secret_id argument), since TF's dependency graph already handles ordering.
- Casing/shape mismatch: CFN props are camelCase strings (secretId, targetId, targetType) referencing a pseudo-resource; TF's SecretsmanagerSecretVersionConfig uses snake_case top-level args (secret_id [required], secret_string, secret_binary, secret_string_wo, secret_string_wo_version, version_stages, region) with the payload as a raw string (typically jsonencode(...) client-side) rather than the structured 3-field CFN shape.
- Unit/behavior mismatch: CFN's 'remove attachment => Secrets Manager strips connection info via PutSecretValue' lifecycle (secretsmanager.generated.d.ts:807) has no TF parallel — destroying an aws_secretsmanager_secret_version just deletes that version; there is no automatic scrubbing of only the connection-info subset of the JSON. Also note CFN allows only one target attachment per secret (line 805); TF does not enforce this.
- RotationSchedule ordering: in CDK, RotationSchedule/secret-rotation recommend depending on the SecretTargetAttachment (rotation-schedule.d.ts:64, secret-rotation.d.ts:115) rather than the bare Secret, because the attachment must complete before rotation is configured. In TF, translate to aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation having an explicit depends_on the aws_secretsmanager_secret_version that carries the connection JSON, preserving the same apply-order guarantee.
- oneToMany=true rationale: no embedded sub-resource blocks exist in CfnSecretTargetAttachmentProps (it is not a strict nested-props split), but functionally two TF resources are needed together — (1) secretsmanager_secret_version to hold the resulting connection JSON, and (2) whichever concrete target resource (rds-cluster, rds-cluster-instance, docdb-cluster, docdbelastic-cluster, redshift-cluster, redshiftserverless-namespace, or db-proxy for the L2 RDS_DB_PROXY case) supplies the attribute values referenced in that JSON. The second resource is an attribute-source SELECTOR that typically already exists in the stack, not a structural child of the attachment.

tfResources.role: primary — the only TF resource; it is the direct 1:1 counterpart to CfnRotationSchedule. secretId -> secretId, rotationLambdaArn -> rotationLambdaArn, rotateImmediatelyOnUpdate -> rotateImmediately, rotationRules.{automaticallyAfterDays,duration,scheduleExpression} -> rotationRules.{automaticallyAfterDays,duration,scheduleExpression} (nested block, not a separate TF resource — TF's rotationRules is a plain sub-object on this same resource just like CFN's, so this is NOT a nested-Cfn-prop-as-standalone-resource case).

attributeNotes:
Mapped (same aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation resource):
- secretId -> secretId : exact match (ARN or name of the secret). Both REQUIRED on their respective props.
- rotationLambdaArn -> rotationLambdaArn : exact match (both optional).
- rotateImmediatelyOnUpdate -> rotateImmediately : renamed (dropped "OnUpdate"), same boolean semantics, both default true.
- rotationRules.automaticallyAfterDays -> rotationRules.automaticallyAfterDays : exact match (number of days).
- rotationRules.duration -> rotationRules.duration : exact match (string window, e.g. "3h" hour-window duration string, no unit conversion needed).
- rotationRules.scheduleExpression -> rotationRules.scheduleExpression : exact match (cron()/rate() expression string).

Shape/requiredness mismatch (VERIFIED):
- In CfnRotationScheduleProps, `rotationRules` is entirely optional (`readonly rotationRules?: ...`) and each sub-field within it is optional. In SecretsmanagerSecretRotationConfig, `rotationRules` is a REQUIRED top-level block (`readonly rotationRules: SecretsmanagerSecretRotationRotationRules;`), even though its own three sub-fields remain optional. When translating a CfnRotationSchedule that omits RotationRules entirely, the TF resource must still receive a `rotationRules = {}` (or equivalent empty block) to satisfy the required-block constraint.
- Casing: standard CFN PascalCase in CloudFormation (AutomaticallyAfterDays, ScheduleExpression, RotateImmediatelyOnUpdate, SecretId) vs TF snake_case in HCL / camelCase in the CDKTF TS binding (automatically_after_days / automaticallyAfterDays, etc.) — mechanical casing difference only, no semantic change except the rotateImmediately(OnUpdate) rename noted above.

Unmappable Cfn props (no equivalent argument on aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation or anywhere else in the AWS TF provider):
- hostedRotationLambda (CfnRotationSchedule.HostedRotationLambdaProperty). Full verified sub-field set: rotationType (required within the struct), kmsKeyArn, masterSecretArn, masterSecretKmsKeyArn, superuserSecretArn, superuserSecretKmsKeyArn, rotationLambdaName, runtime, vpcSecurityGroupIds, vpcSubnetIds, excludeCharacters. (Original mapping's enumeration omitted superuserSecretArn, superuserSecretKmsKeyArn, and runtime — corrected here.) This CFN-only convenience feature auto-provisions a fully managed rotation Lambda via a nested CloudFormation stack (requires `Transform: AWS::SecretsManager-2024-09-16` or -2020-07-23, backed by AWS SAR rotation templates) — Terraform/CDKTF has no equivalent macro. Handling: must be expanded by hand into real, standalone resources — an `aws_lambda_function` (deployed from the appropriate AWS Secrets Manager rotation template/SAR app, or `aws_serverlessapplicationrepository_cloudformation_stack` if consuming the SAR app directly), an `aws_iam_role`/policy for its execution role, optionally `aws_security_group`/VPC config mirroring vpcSecurityGroupIds/vpcSubnetIds, and then pass that Lambda's ARN into `rotationLambdaArn` on aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation. Genuine gap, not a simple rename.
- externalSecretRotationMetadata (Array<CfnRotationSchedule.ExternalSecretRotationMetadataItemProperty {key, value}>) — no TF argument exists for the newer "managed external secret" rotation metadata (used for AWS-owned/partner-managed external secrets). Handling: cannot be represented; if the underlying secret is one of these AWS-managed external secrets, rotation is typically configured on the owning resource (e.g. RDS DBCluster's ManageMasterUserPassword / rotation settings) rather than via a standalone TF secretsmanager_secret_rotation resource — flag for manual review.
- externalSecretRotationRoleArn (string, verified present at CfnRotationScheduleProps line 422) — companion IAM role ARN for the above managed-external-secret rotation; equally unmappable, same handling note (no TF argument; must be handled at the owning-service level, not on this resource).

Extra TF-side fields with no Cfn counterpart (informational, not part of props mapping): `id` (import identifier), `region` (provider region override, standard on all TF resources), and computed read-only `rotationEnabled` attribute.

tfResources.role: primary — sole 1:1 mapping for the whole Cfn resource; CfnResourcePolicyProps has no nested/embedded properties that correspond to separate standalone TF resources

attributeNotes:
Straight 1:1 resource mapping (CfnResourcePolicy -> aws_secretsmanager_secret_policy), 3 config props on each side, all mappable. Verified against secretsmanager.generated.d.ts (CfnResourcePolicyProps L79-104) and secretsmanager-secret-policy/index.d.ts (SecretsmanagerSecretPolicyConfig L7-33).

- secretId (CfnResourcePolicyProps.secretId: `secretsManagerRefs.ISecretRef | string`, required; CFN doc 'The ARN or name of the secret to attach the resource-based policy... we recommend a complete ARN rather than a partial ARN') -> secretArn (SecretsmanagerSecretPolicyConfig.secretArn: string, required). Shape/semantics mismatch: the TF field is named/documented for the ARN specifically (`secret_arn`), whereas Cfn's secretId is looser (name or ARN). When the CDK source passes a bare secret name, the converted code must resolve/pass the secret's ARN (e.g. `secret.secretArn`) into `secretArn`, not the name.

- resourcePolicy (CfnResourcePolicyProps.resourcePolicy: `any | cdk.IResolvable`, required; CFN 'A JSON-formatted string for an AWS resource-based policy') -> policy (SecretsmanagerSecretPolicyConfig.policy: string, required). Casing/type mismatch: Cfn's L1 prop is typed `any` and normally holds a PolicyDocument-like object that CFN serializes for you; Terraform's `policy` field is a plain string, so the converted code must `JSON.stringify()` the policy document before assigning it, or use `cdktn.Fn.jsonencode(...)` if the value is a token.

- blockPublicPolicy (CfnResourcePolicyProps.blockPublicPolicy?: boolean | IResolvable, optional) -> blockPublicPolicy (SecretsmanagerSecretPolicyConfig.blockPublicPolicy?: boolean | cdktn.IResolvable, optional). Clean 1:1, same casing style in JSII binding (block_public_policy in raw HCL/JSON provider schema).

Unmappable / no-op Cfn props:
- attrId (`CfnResourcePolicy.attrId`, the CFN `Id` GetAtt attribute documented as 'The Arn of the secret') — synthesis-time/CloudFormation-only read attribute, not a construction prop, so it has no counterpart in SecretsmanagerSecretPolicyConfig (Config interfaces only carry inputs). Any CDK code that consumed `resourcePolicy.attrId` post-conversion should instead reference the secret's own ARN (e.g. the underlying `secret.secretArn` / the `secretArn` value passed in). The only `id` field present on SecretsmanagerSecretPolicyConfig (`id?: string`, L18) is the unrelated Terraform import-id override input, NOT a computed output; do not conflate the two.
- No CFN Update/DeletionPolicy, Condition, or Metadata props on this L1 (standard cdk.CfnResource base) requiring special handling beyond the normal TerraformMetaArguments (`region`, provider block, etc.) already on SecretsmanagerSecretPolicyConfig.

Confidence: high — resource purpose, cardinality (single secret + single policy document), and all three semantic fields (secret target, policy document, block-public-policy flag) line up cleanly one-to-one with only string-vs-object/ARN-vs-name representational differences to bridge.
